**Findings**

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.assign()` never checks that `model_id` values are unique before building ID-keyed dicts at [bench/dynamic_management.py:456](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L456), [bench/dynamic_management.py:469](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L469), and [bench/dynamic_management.py:496](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L496). With duplicate IDs, later writes overwrite earlier state, and the ID-based filtering at [bench/dynamic_management.py:472](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L472) and [bench/dynamic_management.py:484](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L484) can remove both physical models at once. A runtime probe with input IDs `x, x, y` produced `models_len=3` but only two entries in `role_map`, so one model silently vanished.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reject duplicate or empty `model_id` values at the start of `assign()` and in `DynamicManager.__init__`, raising `ValueError` before any role state is built.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: COL/PAR scoring is normalized against a pool that still includes the locked PM, even though PM is not an eligible COL/PAR candidate. Initial assignment computes `pool_max` once over the full pool at [bench/dynamic_management.py:451](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L451) and then reuses those COL scores at [bench/dynamic_management.py:474](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L474). Reassignment repeats the same pattern at [bench/dynamic_management.py:519](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L519) and [bench/dynamic_management.py:539](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L539). Because normalization is per-dimension, an outlier PM can suppress one dimension for every eligible candidate and reverse the COL winner. I verified this with a 3-model probe where current code chose `b` as COL, but recomputing scores on the non-PM candidates chose `a`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: After PM selection, recompute `pool_max` for COL/PAR on the eligible non-PM set only. In `reassign()`, normalize against the active non-PM candidates, not the full active set.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: `CapabilityFingerprint` has no invariant checks at [bench/dynamic_management.py:254](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L254), yet `_capability_score()` explicitly documents a score in `[0, 1]` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:403](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L403). With mixed-sign raw inputs, `as_normalised_array()` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:278](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L278) can produce `q_tilde` values above `1.0`. A runtime probe using `D_decay=-1.0` alongside a normal peer produced `q=[6,1,1,1]` and a PM capability score of `1.75`, breaking the method’s stated range and distorting role ranking.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `CapabilityFingerprint.__post_init__()` validation for finite, non-negative components, and enforce any true upper bounds that the schema requires. If invalid data still slips through, fail fast rather than letting scores exceed `[0,1]`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: The public ordering API is not a faithful representation of the current role ordering. `capability_scores` is computed once at [bench/dynamic_management.py:453](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L453) and never updated during `reassign()` even though new adjusted COL scores are computed at [bench/dynamic_management.py:533](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L533). `get_ordering()` then just sorts that stale snapshot at [bench/dynamic_management.py:600](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L600), and it also ignores the formal tie-break rule implemented in `_tie_break_key()` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:418](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L418). I verified both failure modes: after penalizing the current COL, `role_map` switched to `par` but `get_ordering(Role.COL)` still showed the old ordering; and swapping the input order of equal-score models flipped `get_ordering()` output.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Recompute ordering on demand from current state, including current candidate set, failure penalty, and tie-break key. If that is not intended, rename this API to something like `get_initial_ordering()` and document it as a construction-time snapshot only.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.33  
DESCRIPTION: `theta_col` is exposed as a configuration knob at [bench/dynamic_management.py:103](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L103), but neither `assign()` nor `reassign()` ever reads it at [bench/dynamic_management.py:428](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L428) or [bench/dynamic_management.py:499](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L499). This is a silent no-op parameter. I verified it by setting `theta_col=0.99` while all COL scores were `0.8`; the code still assigned a COL normally.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement the documented threshold-based COL path or remove `theta_col` from config and docstrings so callers are not misled into thinking it has effect.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.52  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` documents `active_models` as the active set at [bench/dynamic_management.py:510](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L510), but it unconditionally reinserts the locked PM into `new_map` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:524](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L524) even when PM is absent from that set. A direct probe with `active_models={'m2','m3'}` returned `{'pm': PM, 'm2': COL, 'm3': PAR}`. In the full manager flow this may be masked because PM loss appears to abort first at [bench/dynamic_management.py:2950](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2950), so system-level impact is unverified from this scope, but the Area 1 API already violates its own contract.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Treat `pm_model_id not in active_models` as an explicit invalid state and raise, or require callers to include PM and validate that precondition up front.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Scope note: I limited this pass to Area 1 plus the minimal caller context needed to verify behavior, and I intentionally did not restate the already-known stale-live-fingerprint reassignment issue.
